title: Academic Vocabulary: Real vs Pseudo Words
description: Evaluate 18 words to determine which are genuine English words and which are invented pseudo-words (matched to Read and Select screenshot).

words.explanation: 'conducted' is a real English verb meaning organized and carried out (e.g., 'conducted research').
'plorify' is a pseudo-word with no meaning in standard English.
'scrutinize' is a real English verb meaning to examine or inspect closely and thoroughly.
'interruptionist' is an invented pseudo-word; standard English uses 'interrupter'.
'indispensable' is a real English adjective meaning absolutely necessary or essential.
'phenomenon' is a real English noun meaning a remarkable occurrence or observed fact.
'reflact' is an incorrect pseudo-word; the genuine word is 'reflect'.
'ambivalent' is a real English adjective meaning having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas.
'reconsiliate' is a pseudo-word; standard English uses 'reconcile'.
'substantiate' is a real English verb meaning to provide evidence to support or prove the truth of something.
'glimpsy' is an invented pseudo-word; standard English uses 'glimpse' (noun/verb).
'deteriorate' is a real English verb meaning to become progressively worse.
'transcendantalism' is a misspelling/pseudo-form; the correct word is 'transcendentalism'.
'ubiquitous' is a real English adjective meaning present, appearing, or found everywhere.
'compulsation' is an invented pseudo-word; standard English uses 'compulsion'.
'preliminary' is a real English adjective denoting an action or event preceding or preparing for something fuller.
'perplexion' is a pseudo-word; standard English uses 'perplexity'.
